title: Shrimp and Noodles with Mushroom Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp and noodles with mushroom sauce is a dish that combines seafood, pasta, and a savory mushroom cream sauce. The shrimp are usually sautéed until lightly golden, while the noodles (egg or wheat) are cooked al dente. The mushroom sauce adds a smooth, slightly creamy flavor with earthy undertones.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are a high‑protein, low‑calorie seafood, making them popular in health‑focused diets.
Mushrooms naturally contain vitamin D when exposed to ultraviolet light.
The tradition of pairing seafood with noodles originates from Asian cuisines, where the combination is considered harmonious in texture and taste.
A creamy mushroom sauce is often finished with white wine or broth to enhance the mushroom aroma.
The dish can be prepared quickly—typically 20–30 minutes from start to plate.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Shrimp provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat dishes, shrimp contain relatively little saturated fat.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both mushrooms and shrimp supply B‑vitamins such as B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The meal delivers zinc, selenium, and iron, which are important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain noodles adds fiber, aiding digestion and satiety.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should monitor portion size.

items.title: Additives in sauces
items.content: Store‑bought mushroom sauces can contain MSG and preservatives that may not suit everyone.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly stored shrimp can harbor bacteria such as Vibrio, so proper refrigeration is essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté the shrimp in olive oil until pink, then set aside. Cook the noodles separately until al dente. In the same pan, sauté sliced mushrooms, deglaze with a splash of white wine, add cream, salt, pepper, and herbs (parsley, thyme). Toss the noodles and shrimp into the sauce, heat through for 1–2 minutes. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a lemon wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh shrimp refrigerated at 0‑2 °C and use within 2 days; cooked noodles store in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The mushroom sauce can be frozen for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
